clause: §9.2 / §9.4 (reason ∈ too-large|not-pdf|encrypted|read-only|bad-pages|stamp-error; batchFile never throws for a per-file refusal)
claim: A mupdf throw after a successful open (detect/countPages on a damaged page tree at :3328-3330, or saveToBuffer at :3349) escapes batchFile to dispatch's catch, so the reply is ok:false with NO reason. The renderer's batchFailure then writes the raw mupdf message into STATE batch.files[].detail and report.txt, not a §9.2 token. Handles are still balanced.
reproduction: node .quad/scratch/batch/review-engine/probe1.mjs: 'bad tree' bytes (%PDF-1.4 catalog -> /Pages <</Kids[5 0 R]/Count 3>>, obj 5 missing) -> ok false reason undefined error 'Invalid number of pages'; stubbed saveToBuffer throw -> ok false reason undefined 'boom save' (opens 1 destroys 1 both).
fix: In batchFile wrap detect()/countPages() in try -> refuse('not-pdf', message), and wrap pdf.saveToBuffer(SAVE_OPTIONS) in try -> refuse('stamp-error', message, 'save'); or one catch on the outer try returning refuse('not-pdf', message).

clause: §9.5 (checkStampAction BEFORE the transient open), §9.1 (too-large before open), §9.3 (SAVE_OPTIONS not saveOptions(session); MAX_SAVE_BYTES -> too-large)
claim: [fable51 triage: nit upgraded to should — cheap test strength] The behaviour is correct today, but no test pins it, so mutants survive: C (open and destroy a throwaway doc before checkStampAction) 19/19 pass, because (c)/(d) never assert zero opens for a bad action or too-large; L (MAX_SAVE_BYTES check removed) 19/19 pass; and no test runs security-set before batch-file, so a saveOptions(session) leak would go unnoticed.
reproduction: .quad/scratch/batch/review-engine/mutate.sh under run.lock: 'MUTANT C-open-before-check: # pass 19 # fail 0', 'MUTANT L-no-savecap: # pass 19 # fail 0'. probe1.mjs shows the real code is correct: bad action and too-large make 0 opens, a huge save returns too-large and destroys the buffer, and security-set aes-256 then batch gives an output with needsPassword false.
fix: In test (c) record counts.opened before the loop and assert it is unchanged after each bad-action call and after a maxPdfBytes+1 call. In test (a) run security-set {mode:'aes-256', userPassword, ownerPassword} on the open doc before batch-file, then assert the output opens with needsPassword() false.

claim: [fable51 triage: nit upgraded to should — §9.1 says too-large first; move the size checks above checkStampAction] checkStampAction runs before the MAX_PDF_BYTES check, so a buffer that is both too large and paired with a bad action reports stamp-error/invalid-align instead of too-large. Both checks still come before the open, so §9.5 holds.
reproduction: probe1.mjs 'too-large+badalign': new ArrayBuffer(maxPdfBytes+1) with align 'centre' -> reason stamp-error detail invalid-align, opens 0.
fix: Move the bytes instanceof / byteLength > MAX_PDF_BYTES checks above the checkStampAction try block, or accept the order and note it in the contract.

claim: The GUI path resets the Bates counter. #batch-bates-start is prefilled only in openBatchDialog and is never refreshed after a run. startBatch then does `batesNext = Number(start)` with the stale value. A second Start in the same dialog, whether a rerun or a newly picked folder, restarts numbering at 1. The result is duplicate Bates numbers, and STATE shows batch.bates {start:1,next:1} instead of 6/6. The stamp dialog's prefill also drops to 1. The drive does not catch this because driveBatch rewrites the field from batesNext.
reproduction: node .quad/shared/p6/checks/review-batch-renderer-mouse.mjs (under the lock), check A7. Open the dialog from the menu, pick the 4-file folder, set footer 'B-{bates}' with pad 4, click Start (next becomes 6), then click Start again. STATE batch.bates is {start:1,next:1,pad:4}. Screenshot review-batch-a2-done.png shows 'Bates start 1' after the run.
fix: In runBatch's finally, add `batchBatesStartInput.value = String(batesNext); batchBatesPadInput.value = String(batesPad);`. Pin it with a probe or drive that clicks Start twice from the GUI.

claim: #batch-list has no height limit and styles.css has no #batch-dialog rules. With 40 files the dialog's scrollHeight is 1387px in an 860px viewport, so Start and Cancel sit off-screen at y≈1378. During a run the live #batch-summary and the running row scroll out of view, and the human must scroll to reach Cancel.
reproduction: ONLY=b node .quad/shared/p6/checks/review-batch-renderer-mouse.mjs: log line B0 shows '#batch-start before scroll y 1378, hit null'. See screenshot review-batch-b0-running.png.
fix: Wrap the table (or style #batch-list) with max-height:45vh; overflow:auto, and add th/td padding, the same as the #verify-dialog rules in styles.css:1113-1117.

clause: §4.1/§9.16 (align:right action) + review brief (right edges within 10 pt of width−36 incl. rotated.pdf)
claim: The drive half checks each pdf4all-out output only with a text regex. align:right is pinned only as the STATE echo in batch.action and is never checked in the output bytes, so a batch-file that dropped align would still pass every test.
reproduction: .quad/scratch/batch/review-tests/edges.mjs on run-1 outputs: B-0001..B-0005 x1=575.0 on 612-wide pages (w-36=576), including rotated.pdf. That is correct today, but nothing in p6-batch asserts it (grep align/bbox/width finds only the invalid-align engine case at :144).
fix: In the drive test, parse toStructuredText().asJSON() for each output page and assert that the B-000n line's bbox.x+bbox.w is within 10 pt of pageWidth-36 for hello, nav p0-2 and rotated.

claim: The byte-identical check compares the sha of report.txt with the sha of report1, and report1 was read from the same file after all runs finished, so the check always passes. Only the exact-string assert at :316 actually guards against the rerun overwriting the report.
reproduction: Read :315-318: report1 = readFile(out/report.txt) after the whole drive, then sha(out/report.txt) === sha(report1). This holds for any content.
fix: Delete :317-318 and let the exact literal at :316 carry the §9.13 claim, or compare against the sha of the literal expected string and keep a comment that says so.
